headline: Tony Taylor's 12th-inning single walks off the Reds
recap: Tony Taylor's one-out single in the bottom of the 12th scored pinch-runner Denny Doyle and gave the Phillies a 3-2 win over the Cincinnati Reds. Rick Joseph opened the inning with a pinch-hit single, Doyle ran for him, and Larry Bowa's sacrifice bunt moved him into scoring position before Taylor delivered.

Barry Lersch and Tony Cloninger matched each other most of the afternoon. Lersch worked all nine innings for Philadelphia, allowing two runs on eight hits with seven strikeouts and three walks, while Cloninger went eight for Cincinnati, giving up two runs on three hits with four strikeouts and four walks. Neither starter factored in the decision.

Cincinnati's two first-inning runs came around on a third strike that got past catcher Mike Compton, letting Pete Rose score, and a sacrifice fly from Johnny Bench that brought in Bobby Tolan. The Phillies answered with a Don Money double in the second and a Ron Stone single in the seventh, both driving in John Briggs, to force extra innings. Dick Selma threw three scoreless innings in relief to pick up the win; Wayne Granger took the loss for the Reds.
